title: The legal agony of Wile E Coyote
gist: Using the film Coyote vs Acme as a lens, the author argues real civil litigation is decided by disclosure of documentary evidence and settlement dynamics rather than courtroom drama, and that a fast, generous settlement offer from a corporate defendant is itself a signal it is hiding damaging internal information.

insights.claim: The overwhelming majority of civil lawsuits settle before trial as both sides gradually assess the merits of the opposing case, making trial-stage drama rare even when the underlying dispute is significant.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: When evaluating any high-profile corporate lawsuit, expect settlement rather than trial as the base-rate outcome, and treat trial dates as more likely to be pressure points for negotiation than actual courtroom showdowns.
insights.quote: Almost all civil cases settle before trial, as the parties gradually assess the merits of their opponent's cases.
insights.locator: One thing about civil litigation is that it is usually dull

insights.claim: Civil cases are usually decided by documentary evidence that surfaces during pre-trial disclosure/discovery rather than by witness testimony or courtroom performance.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: For investors tracking corporate litigation exposure, the discovery/disclosure phase — not the trial date — is the real event risk to watch for damaging document leaks.
insights.quote: Disclosure of adverse documents can change everything.
insights.locator: But another thing about civil litigation is that it generally comes down to evidence

insights.claim: A corporate defendant that moves quickly to offer a generous settlement in a case that initially looked weak is often doing so because it holds internal information it urgently wants to keep out of discovery, not because it fears losing on the merits.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: A mental model for reading corporate legal behavior: an unusually fast, generous settlement offer against a seemingly weak claim is itself a signal worth investigating, since it often indicates undisclosed liability exposure.
insights.quote: the reason why Acme makes a swift offer of compromise to Coyote and his reluctant lawyer is because it knows it has internal information which it does not want to come out
insights.locator: And the reason why Acme makes a swift offer

insights.claim: A small contingency-based law firm can be pushed to the brink of financial collapse simply by taking on and following through on a single large case against a well-resourced corporate defendant, regardless of the eventual outcome.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Highlights an asymmetry in litigation finance: resource-mismatch alone can make even a promising case financially unsustainable for a small plaintiff-side firm, a factor relevant to litigation-funding investment theses.
insights.quote: The small law firm almost goes bust in following their client's instruction.
insights.locator: Coyote decides to press on with the case

insights.claim: Plaintiffs in civil litigation are frequently pursuing an underlying non-legal objective through the legal process, rather than caring about the litigation or the court's decision itself.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: When assessing why a company or individual is suing, look past the stated legal claim for a collateral strategic goal (reputational, competitive, or personal) that the litigation is really serving.
insights.quote: Civil litigation is about obtaining non-legalistic goals by legalistic methods.
insights.locator: But for Coyote the litigation was merely the means to an end
